documents.unit: Office of the Provost / Academic Senate
documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy (S26-10) - Campus Updates for Students
documents.stance_why: The provost writes "Rules for using AI may vary by course and assignment" and "Your instructors will explain what is permitted", so the document sets no rule itself and hands the decision to instructors.
documents.summary: A provost message to students about the revised Academic Integrity Policy (S26-10). On AI it says rules vary by course, tells students to read syllabi and ask their instructor if unsure, lists AI-literacy resources, and explains the discussion, reporting and appeal steps.

units.why: The provost reports that the Academic Senate "approved an updated Academic Integrity Policy (S26-10)"; this states who adopted the policy, so it is a policy-origin statement (P84), not a rule.
units.anchor: The Academic Senate has approved an updated

units.why: The sentence says the revised policy "responds to ... the growing use of artificial intelligence" while reaffirming honesty and accountability; it states the purpose of the institution-wide policy, which is P56 rather than a specific rule.
units.anchor: responds to changes in teaching, learning, and technology, including

units.why: The justification is that academic integrity ensures "every student is evaluated fairly", a fairness and honest-evaluation reason rather than a skill-building one, so P95.
units.anchor: Academic integrity protects that work and helps ensure that every student is evaluated fairly.

units.why: Students are told that doing "your own work" and following instructor directions meet expectations; this is the ownership-of-work expectation (P29), stated generally rather than AI-specifically.
units.anchor: If you do your own work, follow your instructor
units.frag_start: If you do your own work,
units.fit_note: Generic integrity expectation; the passage does not mention AI itself.

units.why: "Rules for using AI may vary by course and assignment" says the rule is set per course and assignment, which is P04 (and not a university-wide rule).
units.anchor: Rules for using AI may vary by course and assignment.

units.why: Students are told to "read your syllabus and assignment instructions carefully" because "Your instructors will explain what is permitted"; it makes students responsible for learning each course's rules, P78 rather than P10 (which is about asking when unsure).
units.anchor: please read your syllabus and assignment instructions carefully

units.why: "ask your instructor before submitting your work" is advice for students who are unsure whether an AI use or its acknowledgment is allowed, which is exactly P10.
units.anchor: ask your instructor before submitting your work

units.why: The university points students to the "AI Writer's Toolbox" built with the Writing Center to navigate "ethical use of generative and agentic AI tools"; this is a guide resource for students (P70). I chose P70 because the toolbox is an AI-literacy resource.
units.anchor: SJSU provides a number of resources to help students navigate the ethical

units.why: Students "can also book tutoring appointments" at the Writing Center, a pointer to human help alongside AI resources, P72.
units.anchor: where you can also book

units.why: Students "have access to a course on AI Literacy Essentials" from the teaching center; an institution-offered AI-literacy course for students is P70.
units.anchor: Students also have access to a course on

units.why: The Career Center "has numerous training opportunities" to help students use these tools ethically and responsibly; this is a further training offering (P70).
units.anchor: also has numerous training opportunities for students

units.why: Instructors "are expected to discuss the concern with you and explain any proposed academic sanction before reporting"; this is talking with the student before escalating, P57.
units.anchor: Instructors are expected to discuss the concern with you

units.why: "Reports must be submitted within the policy's timeline" is a procedural step for reporting misuse to SCED, P81.
units.anchor: Reports must be submitted within the policy

units.why: "You also have the right to appeal" a sanction, reviewed by a committee giving "an opportunity for you to be heard"; students may respond to sanctions, P64.
units.anchor: You also have the right to appeal if you believe an academic sanction

documents.unit: Office of the Provost / Academic Senate
documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy (S26-10) - Campus Updates for Faculty
documents.stance_why: "Faculty remain responsible for determining whether and how students may use AI tools in their courses", so the document sets no student-facing AI rule and delegates to instructors, while constraining detection and reporting.
documents.summary: A provost message to faculty summarizing four changes in S26-10: mandatory reporting of sanctions, timelines, AI and detection-software guidance, and a sanctioning matrix. AI use is left to instructors, who must state expectations; detector reports cannot be the sole basis for sanctions.

units.why: The provost says integrity ensures "students are evaluated fairly" and that employers and the public "can have confidence" in the degree; the reason is fairness and honest evaluation, P95.
units.anchor: students are evaluated fairly and that employers, graduate schools, and the public can have confidence

units.why: The Academic Senate "approved a revised Academic Integrity Policy (S26-10)" with contributions from faculty, staff and administrators; this describes how and by whom the policy was made, P84.
units.anchor: The Academic Senate has approved a revised

units.why: The policy is said to respond to "valid questions about the efficacy and limitations of AI detection technologies" and to the growth of generative AI; a purpose statement for the revision, P56.
units.anchor: the rapid growth of generative

units.why: "you must report the matter to Student Conduct and Ethical Development (SCED)" is a mandatory procedural step after imposing a sanction, P81.
units.anchor: you must report the matter to Student Conduct and Ethical Development

units.why: "an academic sanction may not be imposed without submitting an Academic Integrity Reporting Form" requires a form before sanctioning; distinct from the duty to report, still P81.
units.anchor: an academic sanction may not be imposed without submitting

units.why: Faculty are "expected to communicate and confer with the student within 10 working days" and before the grade is released; talking with the student first, P57, with a deadline.
units.anchor: expected to communicate and confer with the student within 10 working days
units.frag_start: As a faculty member, you are
units.frag_end: release of the grade for the assessment.
units.fit_note: Adds a 10-working-day deadline and a no-later-than-grade-release limit.

units.why: The report "must be submitted within 15 working days of the incident" with supporting documentation; a formal reporting deadline, P81.
units.anchor: must be submitted within 15 working days of the incident

units.why: "Faculty remain responsible for determining whether and how students may use AI tools in their courses" hands the AI decision to instructors, P04.
units.anchor: Faculty remain responsible for determining whether and how students may use AI tools

units.why: Faculty are told to "communicate those expectations clearly in your syllabi and assignment instructions, including any requirements for acknowledging or citing"; a duty to state AI expectations, P09.
units.anchor: communicate those expectations clearly in your syllabi and assignment instructions
units.frag_end: or citing the use of AI.

units.why: "you may want to use SJSU's AI Policy Builder" offers faculty a tool to craft a course policy, a support for faculty (P63) and optional, so "may".
units.anchor: To craft an AI policy for your course, you may want to use
units.fit_note: A tool for drafting syllabus statements, not a workshop or consultation.

units.why: "Faculty may only use detection services approved by the university" limits which detectors may be used (Turnitin named); nearest type is P92 (approved tools), though it concerns detectors not generative AI tools.
units.anchor: Faculty may only use detection services approved by the university.
units.fit_note: Restricts faculty to university-approved AI-detection services, not generative AI tools for learning.

units.why: "At SJSU, you have access to Turnitin" states which detector the university provides; P40 covers use of detection tools to identify misuse.
units.anchor: At SJSU, you have access to Turnitin.

units.why: Detection tools "have become less effective over time" and may produce false positives, so findings must be approached "with great caution"; detectors are unreliable, P39.
units.anchor: must, however, be approached with great caution
units.frag_start: These detection tools and their findings

units.why: "AI detection reports ... can therefore only be considered alongside other evidence" and "cannot serve as the sole basis for imposing an academic sanction"; detector output as supporting evidence only, P69.
units.anchor: cannot serve as the sole basis for imposing an academic sanction

units.why: The policy lists evidence such as "a significant or noteworthy change from the student's previous work" or inconsistency with class materials; these are kinds of evidence to weigh, P69.
units.anchor: significant or noteworthy change from the student

units.why: S26-10 "introduces a sanctioning matrix with recommended sanctions based on the nature and severity of a violation"; sanctions are set out in advance, nearest type P37.
units.anchor: sanctioning matrix with recommended sanctions based on the nature and severity of a violation
units.fit_note: The matrix gives recommended, not fixed, sanctions; the passage does not list the penalties.

units.why: "The matrix is a guide, not a substitute for faculty judgment" keeps discretion with the instructor while aiming at consistency; part of how sanctions are stated, P37.
units.anchor: The matrix is a guide, not a substitute for faculty judgment.
units.fit_note: Concerns discretion over a recommended matrix, not a stated penalty.

units.why: CFETI "can provide you with relevant AI Pedagogical Resources" and offers consultations for faculty, programs and departments; support for faculty, P63.
units.anchor: The Center offers in-person and Zoom consultations for individual faculty members

units.why: CFETI will help faculty "better understand the effectiveness, limits, and drawbacks of tools such as Turnitin" and hosts a Turnitin Clarity workshop; faculty learning support, P63.
units.anchor: better understand the effectiveness, limits, and drawbacks of tools such as Turnitin

units.why: "please review the revised policy, update your course materials as needed" asks faculty to stay current and update their materials; staying informed, P102.
units.anchor: please review the revised policy, update your course materials as needed

documents.title: Developing a Generative AI Syllabus Policy
documents.stance_why: "Faculty may allow, restrict, or prohibit the use of generative AI depending on the course and assignment" leaves the decision to instructors and lists three approaches, so it delegates.
documents.summary: A library guide for faculty that cites S26-10 as requiring syllabus AI statements and points to CFETI tools (AI Policy Builder, SAID). Instructors choose to allow, restrict or prohibit and must say so in syllabus and assignments.

units.why: The guide says S26-10 "requires instructors to communicate their course policy regarding the use of artificial intelligence ... in the syllabus"; this is the syllabus statement requirement, P09.
units.anchor: requires instructors to communicate their course policy regarding the use of artificial intelligence

units.why: The CFETI "AI Policy Builder" lets faculty "create or customize a syllabus statement using approaches that allow, restrict, or prohibit" AI; a three-way set of approaches, P05, with the tool itself supporting faculty.
units.anchor: approaches that allow, restrict, or prohibit generative AI use
units.frag_start: Create or customize a syllabus statement
units.fit_note: Names three approaches (allow, restrict, prohibit) via a builder tool, without defining levels.

units.why: "SAID (Student AI Disclosure)" is a resource "faculty can use to help students document how they used AI"; student documentation of AI use, nearest P26.
units.anchor: A resource faculty can use to help students document how they used AI
units.fit_note: A disclosure resource offered to instructors; the passage does not require students to submit transcripts.

units.why: "Faculty may allow, restrict, or prohibit the use of generative AI depending on the course and assignment" is the decide-per-instructor rule, P04.
units.anchor: Faculty may allow, restrict, or prohibit the use of generative AI

units.why: "communicate expectations clearly in both the syllabus and assignment instructions" is a duty to state AI expectations in both places, P09.
units.anchor: communicate expectations clearly in both the syllabus and assignment instructions

documents.title: Academic Integrity (School of Information)
documents.date_or_term: undated; cites the ChatGPT Sep 14 2023 version
documents.stance_why: "The use of ChatGPT and any other AI-assisted software must be cited as a reference source" allows use and sets a citation condition, so the stance is permit with conditions.
documents.summary: The iSchool one-paragraph AI policy (v1, Sept 2023): any AI-assisted software must be cited in APA style, failure to cite is a violation, and uncertain students should confer with the instructor. The rest of the page is generic integrity and sanction procedure.

units.why: The page gives "v1 adopted on September 14, 2023" for the "AI Assisted Software Academic Integrity Policy"; the adoption date and version describe when the policy was made, P84.
units.anchor: v1 adopted on September 14, 2023

units.why: "The use of ChatGPT and any other AI-assisted software must be cited as a reference source" requires students to cite any AI use, P24.
units.anchor: must be cited as a reference source

units.why: The citation rule is justified as "consistent with the requirement to cite reference and quotations where ideas and sentences are used from other sources"; AI is treated like any other outside source, P45.
units.anchor: consistent with the requirement to cite reference and quotations
units.frag_start: to be consistent with the requirement

units.why: "Failure to cite the use of any AI-assisted software constitutes a violation of SJSU policy F15-7 and the School of Information's academic integrity policy"; non-citation itself is the violation, P28 (also misconduct, P36, but the focus is the disclosure duty).
units.anchor: Failure to cite the use of any AI-assisted software constitutes a violation of SJSU policy

units.why: "If students are uncertain ... it is their responsibility to confer with the instructor" tells students to ask the instructor when unsure about AI use, P10.
units.anchor: it is their responsibility to confer with the instructor of that particular course
units.frag_start: If students are uncertain as to how

units.why: The APA instructions say how to cite AI-assisted software, naming the tool, year and model version (e.g. "OpenAI. (2023). ChatGPT (Sep 14 version)"); tool and date details, P25, though no prompt or output is required.
units.anchor: In the APA editorial style, you are to cite the use of AI-Assisted software
units.fit_note: Specifies APA format with tool and version/date; does not require the prompt or output.

units.why: Once an incident is determined, "A report of the incident must be sent to the Office of Student Conduct & Ethical Development"; this sits in the general plagiarism procedures that the AI-citation violation falls under, P81.
units.anchor: A report of the incident must be sent to the Office of Student Conduct
units.fit_note: Generic integrity-reporting rule, not specific to AI.

units.why: The page lists options such as "lower a grade", "assign a zero", "assign an F" for plagiarized work and says "willingness to admit to infraction is an important factor"; concrete penalties from the general plagiarism section that cover uncited AI, P37.
units.anchor: an instructor has the following options if they determine that student work has been plagiarized
units.fit_note: Generic plagiarism sanctions, not AI-specific; also notes student admission as a mitigating factor.

notes: Coder B. The S26-10 policy PDF itself was not in the saved texts; provost summaries only. The two provost texts carry heavy navigation boilerplate (skipped). iSchool generic plagiarism procedure units (report, sanction options) were coded because uncited AI falls under them; they are not AI-specific.
